obligation: Card brand notice: Visa account data compromise
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, Visa Supplemental Requirements v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 to A.4
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa payment account data or to a system that stores, processes, or transmits it
deadline: Report to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation; incident report within 3 calendar days after notifying Visa; at-risk account numbers within 3 calendar days of discovery, of Visa's request, or of setting the window of exposure
notify: Visa (through the sponsor banks and Visa's case management tool); acquiring banks immediately
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Payment Processing division stores, processes, and transmits Visa account data; the gateway transmits it
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)
clock_starts: Reasonable suspicion anywhere in the group (POL-03 4.4)

obligation: Card brand notice: other brands
citation: Each card brand's account data compromise rules
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per each brand's rules (timing not verified in this sample; confirm with the sponsor banks)
notify: Each brand through the sponsor banks
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow each brand's rules
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)

obligation: Sponsor bank contract notice of suspected account data compromise
citation: Sponsor agreements (contract); Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3
trigger: Suspected or confirmed account data compromise
deadline: Within 24 hours (sponsor agreements); immediately (Visa)
notify: Each of the four sponsor banks' designated security and compliance contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all four banks
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Banks A and B (OCC)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to the bank for four or more hours. Covered services: clearing, settlement, reconciliation, and merchant funding files (sponsor agreements; 12 U.S.C. 1867(c)). Excludes previously communicated maintenance, testing, or updates (53.4(b))
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact; if none on file (Bank B today), the bank's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility (53.4(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to two national banks. Card data theft alone does not trigger it; containment that halts covered services for 4 or more hours does
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)
clock_starts: Determination that covered services are or are reasonably likely to be disrupted 4+ hours

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Bank C (Federal Reserve)
trigger: Same trigger as 53.4 for a Board-supervised banking organization customer (state member bank)
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank C's designated point of contact (on file)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Bank C is a state member bank (225.300(c); 225.301(b)(1))
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Bank D (FDIC)
trigger: Same trigger as 53.4 for an FDIC-supervised institution customer (state nonmember bank)
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank D's designated point of contact; none on file today (POAM-005), so its CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility (304.24(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Bank D is a state nonmember bank (304.21(c); 304.22(b)(1))
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (the sponsor banks' own duty)
trigger: Notification incident at a banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident occurred
notify: Each bank's primary federal regulator (by the bank)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the banks' duty. The division's prompt notice gives each bank what it needs for its own decision

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event: Payment Processing
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without the individual's authorization (unauthorized access presumed to be acquisition absent reliable evidence otherwise) involving the information of at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: Federal Trade Commission, through the electronic form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - financial institution under 16 CFR 314. Affected cardholders are counted toward the 500 (conservative reading; counsel confirms)
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event: Software division
trigger: Same trigger, for customer information held by the gateway or commerce software
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - treated as a financial institution on a conservative reading
notifying_entity: Software division (client trust and assurance director)

obligation: FTC notice law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official provides a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after notice to the FTC; up to 60 more days on written request; further delay only if FTC staff agrees
notify: Include in the FTC notice; the FTC contacts the official
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Merchant Consulting notice to the Payment Processing division (service provider)
citation: Intercompany services agreement (2025; safeguards and notice clause being added, POAM-009); 16 CFR 314.4(f)(2)
trigger: Security event affecting customer information or account data that consulting handles for the processor
deadline: Within 24 hours (amended term); today no contractual clock, so the group SOC applies POL-03 4.1 (1 hour)
notify: Payment Processing division CISO; head of bank and network relationships
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consulting is a service provider (314.2(r))

obligation: Third-party agent notice to merchants (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of a system maintained for merchants (covered entities) involving personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected merchant, with all information it needs for its own notices; the division may send notices for the merchant (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the processor (and consulting for its clients) is a third-party agent for merchants' cardholder data. Florida's definition counts a card number only with any required security code, access code, or password; counsel applies each state's definition
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (covered entity duty)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents where a group entity is the covered entity (for example merchant owner data), or when sending notices for a merchant
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days with good cause given in writing to the department, for this notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when a group entity owns the data or sends notices for a merchant

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents and a group entity is the covered entity (otherwise the merchant's duty)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents; definitions and third-party agent rules vary
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Merchants and clients (as data owners); residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - merchants and cardholders in all 50 states; apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: ISV notice (Software division)
trigger: Security incident affecting ISV credentials or ISV data
deadline: Within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
notifying_entity: Software division (client trust and assurance director)
clock_starts: Software division learns of the incident

obligation: Enterprise merchant notice (Software division)
trigger: Security incident affecting the merchant's data
deadline: Within 48 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
notifying_entity: Software division (client trust and assurance director)
clock_starts: Software division learns of the incident

obligation: Merchant contract notice (Payment Processing)
trigger: Security incident affecting merchant or cardholder data
deadline: Per the merchant agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
notifying_entity: Payment Processing (head of bank and network relationships)

obligation: Consulting client notice
trigger: Confirmed incident affecting client data
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SOC 2 user entity communications
citation: SOC 2 system description commitments; terms of service (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting the commitments described in the SOC 2 report
deadline: Per the commitments (without undue delay)
notify: Merchants and ISVs using SYS-S1 and SYS-S2
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
notifying_entity: Software division (client trust and assurance director)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay possible only on U.S. Attorney General finding)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded holding company

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report on Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describes risk management, strategy, and governance; consider the incident when drafting

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an extortion demand is made

obligation: Voluntary law enforcement and CISA report
trigger: Criminal compromise of payment data
deadline: As soon as practicable; coordinate with counsel and the PFI
notify: U.S. Secret Service or FBI field office; IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: SCI event notification
trigger: SCI event at an SCI entity
deadline: Immediately; written notice within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity is an SCI entity

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: No later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity is a credit union

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity holds federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity holds federal contracts or subcontracts
